title: Servable quality declarations and fallback scheduling policy
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: Establish a canonical SLI/SLO declaration and an operator-friendly fallback scheduling policy per servable (endpoint/model variant) that ties error budget arithmetic to multi-region failover decisions, circuit-breaker thresholds, and tiered load-shedding. Outcome: a single machine-readable manifest and an operational playbook used by the routing controller and the console to automate graceful degradations while preserving critical SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Machine-readable servable SLO manifest schema accepted by runtime and console; 2) Routing controller implements priority-aware fallback and records events to the SLO ledger; 3) Grafana dashboard surfaces per-servable SLI burn, remaining error budget, and active failover reasons; 4) Runbook created with circuit-breaker tuning guide and post-failover mitigation steps; 5) Smoke tests showing controlled failover during simulated regional capacity loss.
notes: SLIs defined: availability (5xx-free requests), median p95 latency for gen endpoints, quality SLI for classification/regression routes measured via promptset sampling.
Default SLO bands: availability 99.9% monthly, latency p95 <= 300ms for latency-sensitive routes, response-quality fidelity >= 96% on eval promptset.
Error budget policy: automatic borrowing allowed within same tenancy up to 10% of allocation; cross-region borrowing requires explicit arming by on-call manager.
Fallback ordering: warm-standby variant -> quantized cheaper variant -> regional replica in secondary region -> degraded-mode with truncated context and early stop tokens.
Circuit breakers: trip on sustained 30m burn-rate > 3x baseline OR instantaneous tail-error spike causing >2% 5xx traffic; hysteresis includes 10m cooldown before attempt to reclose.
Load-shedding matrix: prioritize background embedding and batch jobs for shedding before dropping low-latency read routes; token-budget-aware shed decisions taken per-client token-velocity.
Operational signals: existing telemetry (trace_id, route, tenant, variant, region) augmented with 'rollback_cause' and 'eviction_reason' tags for postmortem attribution.
Telemetry emits 'slo_ledger' events to metrics topic with fields (servable_key, window_start, window_end, sli_value, error_budget_remaining, fallback_action).
Security: manifests signed by control-plane key; manifests for Private deployments validated by KMS-integrated attestation flow.
